clips.answer: It's ongoing research at the University of Toronto on safe driving, which I'm co-developing. clips.question: How does Talkback avoid spoilers?

clips.answer: A character never gets text you haven't reached. Our server only hands it the passages and summaries up to your current position, and characters you haven't met yet stay locked. We enforce that rule in the backend with unit tests, and retrieval runs on Vertex AI Vector Search over only the passages already read. We measured spoiler leaks with an LLM judge evaluation.

clips.answer: It's a text-to-SQL layer that retrieves business logic, not just schema, because a schema says what a column is called, not what it means. clips.question: How does text2sql-memory learn from corrections?
paraphrases: How do user corrections become rules?
How does the system improve when someone says the SQL is wrong?
What stops one bad correction from breaking the knowledge store?

clips.answer: When someone corrects an answer, the system distils that correction into at most three general rules, which start out as drafts. A correction never edits an existing rule, so one bad correction can't overwrite knowledge that already works. A draft is promoted to reviewed only once two answers citing it are marked good, and only a person can certify it.

clips.answer: It's a question answering tool over a fixed reading list of arXiv papers, where every claim cites the exact paper and section. Papers are parsed from their LaTeX source, chunked by section, and searched with BM25 plus optional e5 embeddings. The model must quote what it cites, and any quote missing from that passage is flagged, though that doesn't prove the passage supports the claim.

clips.answer: In my arXiv Paper RAG project, the model must quote the passage it cites, and code checks that the quote appears there. A quote that isn't found gets flagged, as does a citation marker with no matching citation. Retrieved text is treated as untrusted, so the model is told not to follow instructions inside it. The honest limit: this proves the quote exists, not that the passage supports the claim.

clips.answer: Undercurrent is a commodity forecasting project with Unilever Horizon3 Labs, and we're a team of four. The question is whether a time-series foundation model beats a domain model on commodity prices, so we benchmark zero-shot Chronos-2 against a hierarchical Bayesian driver model. We also fuse both with Bayesian Predictive Synthesis and score leakage-safe probabilistic forecasts on CRPS and calibration. There's no public code or results to share.

clips.answer: It was a two-person course project at UBC in early 2026, built on routine health checkup data that mixes structured lab values with free-text organ reports. We used a variational autoencoder to compress more than 18,000 sparse features into a 32-dimensional latent space, then ran K-Means on it. That recovered seven clinical phenotypes, like sensorineural hearing loss, liver fibrosis and hypothyroidism, with no labels at all.
